doc.catalog.title: Components
doc.catalog.intro: Browse components — one page per component, like m3.material.io.
doc.quick-start.title: Quick Start
doc.quick-start.blurb: Install and use K3ui web components in Angular, React, Vue, or plain HTML.
doc.quick-start.intro: Pick a path that matches your stack. CDN for a quick try in plain HTML, npm when you already have a bundler, or the framework notes for Angular, React, and Vue. After install, call K3UI.init once, import k3ui.css, and register only the components you use so first paint stays light.
doc.quick-start.cdn.title: CDN — no build step
doc.quick-start.cdn.blurb: Import the bundle from a CDN. Works in any modern browser with no tooling.
doc.quick-start.npm.title: Install via package manager
doc.quick-start.npm.blurb: Add the package, import CSS + init, then use the tags in your app.
doc.quick-start.angular.title: Angular
doc.quick-start.angular.blurb: Add CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA so unknown k3-* tags are allowed.
doc.quick-start.react.title: React
doc.quick-start.react.blurb: React 19+ supports Custom Elements natively. Prefer refs for custom events.
doc.quick-start.vue.title: Vue
doc.quick-start.vue.blurb: Vue supports Custom Elements natively — use @click and v-model where needed.
doc.material-symbols.title: Material Symbols
doc.material-symbols.blurb: Browse the Material Symbols catalog — search, categories, Outlined · Rounded · Sharp, FILL / Weight / Grade / Optical Size. Click an icon to copy a K3ui ligature snippet.
doc.material-symbols.intro: K3ui uses Material Symbols ligatures via data-k3-icon (no ms-icon package). This browser loads the variable fonts (Material Symbols New) so you can tune FILL, wght, GRAD, and opsz live — click an icon to copy a Translate-safe snippet.
doc.material-symbols.error: Could not load the icon catalog.
doc.gestures.title: Gestures
doc.gestures.blurb: Tap · long-press · swipe · pan · rotate · scale · repeat · sequence — detectGesture or k3-*-gesture.
doc.gestures.intro: Gesture helpers detect tap, long-press, swipe, pan, rotate, scale, repeat, and sequences via detectGesture or k3-*-gesture events. Listen for start · update · end · cancel phases, tune thresholds to the interaction, and always provide a non-gesture fallback for accessibility.
doc.gestures.section.basic.blurb: Phases start · update · end · cancel. Use phase() handlers or listen to k3-gesture.
doc.gestures.section.sequence.blurb: Ordered chain — tap, then swipe within 800 ms.
doc.keyboard.title: Keyboard
doc.keyboard.blurb: Press · release · chords (2–3+ keys) — attachKeyboard · bindChord · K3UI.keyboard.
doc.keyboard.intro: Track key down/up, held sets, and multi-key chords via attachKeyboard or bindChord / bindChords (K3UI.keyboard). Normalize keys to stable ids, ignore fields when binding shortcuts, and prefer chord strings like control+shift+k over raw KeyboardEvent checks.
doc.keyboard.section.downup.blurb: Focus the pad · hold keys — log shows down / up and the pressed set.
doc.keyboard.section.chords.blurb: Try Control+K or Control+Shift+K — fires once when the last key completes the chord.
doc.keyboard.section.bind.blurb: One-shot helpers for shortcut maps — ignoreFields skips inputs.
doc.keyboard-media.title: Media hotkeys
doc.keyboard-media.blurb: Space/K · ←/→ · N/P · M — bindMediaHotkeys on top of K3UI.keyboard (powers k3-audio-player).
doc.keyboard-media.intro: Media shortcuts reuse the keyboard utility: Space/K toggle, arrows seek, N/P next/prev, M mute. They only fire when hotkeys is set and the player is visible (hidden playground pages never steal keys). bindMediaHotkeys skips focused fields.
doc.keyboard-media.section.map.blurb: Default seek step ±5 s — override with seekStepSec.
doc.keyboard-media.section.player.blurb: Focus the page (not a field) · Space pauses · arrows seek · M mutes.
doc.mouse.title: Mouse
doc.mouse.blurb: Buttons · move · drag · wheel · click — attachMouse · K3UI.mouse.
doc.mouse.intro: attachMouse tracks button down/up, move, click, double-click, wheel, enter/leave, and dragstart/drag/dragend with thresholds. Prefer Pointer Events when available; use button ids left · middle · right · back · forward.
doc.mouse.section.pad.blurb: Move, click, drag, and scroll over the pad — phases stream below.
doc.mouse.section.buttons.blurb: left · middle · right · back · forward — buttons bitfield helpers included.
doc.dnd.title: Drag & drop
doc.dnd.intro: Drag-and-drop primitives power sortable lists and typed drop targets through attachSortable, attachDraggable, and attachDroppable (K3UI.dnd). Reuse the same engine as sortable chip-sets, announce drop success, and keep keyboard alternatives for reordering.
doc.dnd.section.sortable.blurb: Reorder siblings — same engine as k3-chip-set sortable.
doc.dnd.section.drop.blurb: Typed payload k3/demo — hover highlights the zone.
doc.scrollbar.title: Scrollbar
doc.scrollbar.blurb: Discreet edge scrollbar — .k3-scroll · edgeScrollbarStyles (no Windows arrows).
doc.scrollbar.intro: K3 scrollbars stay discreet on the edge — a slim thumb without Windows arrows. Apply .k3-scroll in light DOM or edgeScrollbarStyles inside shadow roots, override size tokens when needed, and pad an inner child instead of fighting WebKit scrollbar-width.
doc.scrollbar.section.demo.blurb: Thumb flush to the right edge · 6dp · transparent track.
doc.scrollbar.section.usage.blurb: Shadow CE → edgeScrollbarStyles + class k3-scroll. Light DOM → global .k3-scroll from k3ui.css.
doc.scrollbar.section.tokens.blurb: Override --k3-scroll-size and --k3-scroll-track-inset on the scrollport. For rounded panels, set track-inset ≥ border-radius so the thumb never cuts the curve.
doc.scrollbar.section.rules.blurb: Pad an inner child · never set scrollbar-width on WebKit with ::-webkit-scrollbar.
doc.scrollbar.demo.line: Line {n} — scroll to see the edge thumb.
doc.button.title: Buttons
doc.button.blurb: Filled · tonal · elevated · outlined · text. Press morphs radius only.
doc.button.intro: Buttons communicate actions a user can take. Prefer filled for the primary action on a screen, tonal for secondary emphasis, elevated when the button sits on a busy surface, outlined for quiet alternatives, and text for the lowest emphasis. Material 3 Expressive morphs corner radius on press without changing the layout size — keep labels short, pair with a clear icon when helpful, and reserve one filled button per view.
doc.ripple.title: Ripple
doc.ripple.blurb: Classic Material ink — circular press from the pointer + hover state layer.
doc.ripple.intro: Ripple is the classic Material ink response: a circular highlight expands from the pointer while a state layer covers hover and focus. Host it on a position:relative overflow-hidden surface. Buttons and many interactive components already include it — use the standalone tag when you build custom pressable chrome.
doc.ripple.section.demo.blurb: Press and hold — ink grows from the contact point (Material Web parity).
doc.ripple.section.usage.blurb: Place inside a position:relative surface. Buttons include it by default.
doc.shape-chip.title: Shape Chip
doc.shape-chip.blurb: Pill + leading Material shape — informative legends and color cues.
doc.shape-chip.intro: Shape Chip is a custom K3ui action: a pill label with a Material shape whose center sits on the leading edge. It is not an M3 Chip and not an Input — use it as an informative legend where the shape carries the color. Optional icon via slot="icon". Add toggle only when selection is needed.
doc.shape-chip.section.sizes.blurb: XS · SM · MD · LG · XL — same height ladder as Buttons; shape & icon scale with the pill.
doc.icon-button.title: Buttons Icon
doc.icon-button.blurb: Icon buttons help people take minor actions with a single tap — ideal when space is tight and the action is clear from the icon alone.
doc.icon-button.intro: Use them in app bars, toolbars, cards, and media controls. Choose a color style by emphasis: filled for the highest, then tonal, outlined, and standard for the lowest. Material 3 Expressive adds five sizes, round or square shapes, and narrow, default, or wide widths — with shape morph on press and when selected. Toggle icon buttons hold a binary state such as favorite or mute; prefer an outlined icon when off and a filled one when on. Always provide an accessible name that describes the action, not the glyph, and keep a ≥48dp touch target on extra-small and small sizes.
doc.usage.title: Usage
doc.usage.blurb: Copy-paste snippets to drop this component into a project — HTML, optional CSS, and JS init.
doc.icon-button.usage.blurb: Copy-paste snippets to drop k3-icon-button into a project — HTML markup, optional CSS, and JS init + toggle listener.
doc.fab.title: FAB
doc.fab.intro: A floating action button highlights the single most important action on a screen. Use default, medium, or large icon-only sizes and keep the glyph unmistakable. Place it where the thumb can reach it, avoid stacking multiple FABs, and prefer an extended FAB when a short label removes ambiguity.
doc.fab.section.sizes.blurb: Default · Medium · Large — 56 · 80 · 96 dp (M3 Expressive; not the XS–XL button ladder).
doc.extended-fab.title: FAB Extended
doc.extended-fab.intro: Extended FABs pair an icon with a short label for actions that need a word, not only a glyph. Keep the label to one or two words, use them sparingly, and collapse back to an icon-only FAB when the layout becomes compact or the action is already well known.
doc.extended-fab.section.sizes.blurb: Small · Medium · Large — 40 · 56 · 96 dp height (M3 Expressive FAB ladder).
doc.fab-menu.title: FAB Menu
doc.fab-menu.blurb: Material 3 Expressive FAB menu — labeled pills from the trailing edge, Default · Medium · Large trigger, close FAB Default. Replaces speed dials.
doc.fab-menu.intro: The Material 3 Expressive FAB menu replaces speed dials with labeled pills that expand from the trailing edge. Offer a small set of related actions, keep one menu size, and use the Default close FAB so dismissal stays obvious. Prefer this pattern when several peer actions share equal weight.
doc.fab-menu.hint.below: Same cases · FAB on top · menu below · start edge · inverted open · Default 56 · Medium 80 · Large 96.
doc.button-group.title: Buttons Group
doc.button-group.blurb: Standard & connected — M3 Expressive (gaps, shapes, toggle colors).
doc.button-group.intro: Button groups present related choices as a single control. Standard groups keep a visible gap and morph round↔square on select; connected groups sit nearly flush with shared seams. Use single selection for exclusive modes and multi for independent toggles. Match size to the surrounding chrome and keep the group label for accessibility.
doc.button-group.hint.standard: Gap XS 18 · SM 12 · MD/LG/XL 8 · press +15% (neighbors) · round↔square on select.
doc.button-group.hint.connected-round: Gap 2dp · outer CornerFull · inner 4/8/8/16/20 · selected stadium · no width morph.
doc.button-group.hint.connected-square: Gap 2dp · outer 4/8/8/16/20 (first/last) · facing seams 4dp · selected = color only.
doc.button-group.hint.sizes-standard: Larger gap on XS/SM (18 / 12 dp) on purpose — keeps ≥48 dp touch targets. MD/LG/XL = 8 dp. Not connected (2 dp).
doc.button-group.hint.sizes-connected: Connected stays 2dp; corner tokens scale XS→XL.
doc.button-group.hint.labels: labels=selected — icon always, label when checked.
doc.button-menu.title: Buttons Menu
doc.button-menu.intro: A button menu opens a list of actions from a single trigger. Use it when space is limited and the actions are secondary. Keep the menu short, order items by frequency, and mirror the trigger variant so the control feels native to the toolbar or card that hosts it.
doc.button-pill.title: Buttons Pill
doc.button-pill.blurb: Destination pill — vertical (icon + label below) · horizontal (icon + label inline).
doc.button-pill.intro: Button Pill is the shared destination chrome used by navigation rail (collapsed / expanded) and navigation bar (vertical / horizontal). Vertical puts a 56×32 indicator behind the icon with the label underneath; horizontal wraps icon and label in a 56dp pill. Selected uses secondary-container with a scaleX spring. Not wired into nav yet — ready to drop in.
doc.button-pill.section.layouts.blurb: Single-select like nav — click a destination. 1 vertical · 2 horizontal.
doc.button-pill.section.stretch.blurb: Horizontal + stretch — full-width row (rail expanded). Click to select.
doc.button-arrow.title: Buttons Arrow
doc.button-arrow.blurb: Split chevrons — horizontal or vertical · filled · tonal · outlined · cyclic list.
doc.button-arrow.intro: Arrow buttons step through a cyclic list with paired chevrons. Use horizontal for carousels and vertical for stacked pages. Keep the list short, surface the current value nearby, and match filled, tonal, or outlined to nearby controls.
doc.button-card.title: Buttons Card
doc.button-card.blurb: Compact link row — tonal icon well · label · subtitle · optional href.
doc.button-card.intro: Button cards present a short destination with an icon, a primary label, and an optional subtitle. Use them in grids for peer links. Tint the icon well with --k3-button-card-icon-bg and --k3-button-card-icon-fg; pass href for navigation.
playground.social.title: Find K3ui
playground.social.blurb: Follow along on your favorite platforms.
doc.button-grid.title: Buttons Grid
doc.button-grid.blurb: 3×3 Expressive pad — FAB reveal or always-open · filled · tonal · outlined.
doc.button-grid.intro: Button Grid offers nine peer actions in a compact 3×3. FAB mode expands from a centre trigger; pad mode stays open. Prefer short labels, one clear primary set, and filled, tonal, or outlined to match the surface.
doc.button-pad.title: Buttons Pad
doc.button-pad.blurb: Four-way pad — diagonal or cardinal · filled · tonal · outlined.
doc.button-pad.intro: Button Pad maps four directions for navigation or pan. Diagonal keeps compass corners; cardinal rotates the grid 45° for up/right/down/left. Use it for maps, galleries, and spatial UIs — keep one pad per view.
doc.button-smart.title: Buttons Smart
doc.button-smart.blurb: Quick Settings tile — pill ↔ squircle morph · marquee label · light haptic.
doc.button-smart.intro: Smart buttons mirror Material You Quick Settings tiles: off is a charcoal pill, on morphs to a squircle on primary-container. Pair an icon with a short label, optional subtitles, and a two-column grid for denser control strips.
doc.fab-dial.title: FAB Dial
doc.fab-dial.blurb: Speed dial — flower fan · corner dock · up to four actions.
doc.fab-dial.intro: FAB Dial fans related actions from a single FAB in a radial flower. Keep icons unmistakable, dismiss with scrim or Escape, and avoid stacking with another open dial. For a linear stack (including vertical), use FAB Rail.
doc.fab-rail.title: FAB Rail
doc.fab-rail.blurb: Speed dial — linear rail along an axis · auto-fit · up to five actions.
doc.fab-rail.intro: FAB Rail expands actions in a straight line from the trigger. Choose direction by corner, let auto-fit scale for short viewports, and keep labels optional. Use when order matters more than a radial fan.
doc.counter.title: Counter
doc.counter.blurb: − / value / + pill — XS–XL · step · negatives · disabled · drag spinbutton.
doc.counter.intro: Counters adjust a numeric value with decrement, display, and increment. Five Expressive sizes keep the pill aligned with nearby buttons. Set step (e.g. 10), bounds, decimals, allow-negative, or disabled; the centre spinbutton supports drag to nudge the value.
doc.signature.title: Signature
doc.signature.blurb: Canvas pad — pen · initials · PNG / SVG · clear · touch.
doc.signature.intro: The signature pad captures strokes with pointer or touch. Line width follows velocity (SignaturePad). Type initials and confirm to stamp them; Clear resets. Export as a data URL or SVG; disable or set readonly to freeze the result.
doc.signature.section.examples.blurb: Default · primary ink · disabled — initials + Clear under each pad.
doc.autocomplete.title: Autocomplete
doc.autocomplete.blurb: Editable combobox — filterable listbox · lazy k3-query · outlined field.
doc.autocomplete.intro: Autocomplete pairs a text field with a filterable option list. Users type to narrow choices or pick from the panel; use k3-query to load options asynchronously. Match variant and supporting text to neighboring fields, and commit selection with k3-change.
doc.wheel-picker.title: Wheel picker
doc.wheel-picker.blurb: Arcade-style rotating columns — initials · submit · preview.
doc.wheel-picker.intro: Wheel picker spins independent character columns for arcade-style entry. Set length and allowed characters, optionally show a live preview and submit button. Listen for k3-change while spinning and k3-submit when the user confirms.
doc.button-segmented.title: Buttons Segmented
doc.button-segmented.blurb: M3E segmented control — single or multi-select · check mark · rounded or square.
doc.button-segmented.intro: Segmented buttons switch between a small set of related views or filters. Define segments as JSON, choose single or multi-select, and optionally show a check on the active segment. Use rounded for pill chrome or square for denser toolbars.
doc.bubble.title: Bubble
doc.bubble.blurb: Chat row — start/end placement · body colors · image, header, footer slots.
doc.bubble.intro: Bubbles layout conversation messages with optional avatar, header metadata, body text, and footer status. Align incoming messages to the start and outgoing to the end; pick a body color for emphasis or semantic tone.
doc.quote.title: Quote
doc.quote.blurb: Testimonial card — tilted surface · primary offset · author | citation split.
doc.quote.intro: Quotes present a short citation beside the author (avatar, name, role) on a tilted surface with a colored offset layer. Flip columns with layout author-end; motion deepens the tilt on hover only. Add an optional action link for “Read more”.
doc.quote.demo.body1: Dynamic theme tokens keep this testimonial card on-brand without hard-coded accents.
doc.quote.demo.body2: Invert the columns with layout author-end — citation first, avatar on the right.
doc.codeblock.title: Code block
doc.codeblock.blurb: Syntax-highlighted sample — copy · download · collapsible toolbar.
doc.codeblock.intro: Code blocks present highlighted snippets with an optional toolbar for copy and download. Pass source via the default slot or the code property, set language for highlighting, and collapse long samples automatically or with collapsible.
doc.carousel.title: Carousel
doc.carousel.blurb: M3 Expressive — multi-browse · hero · uncontained · full-screen · loop + indicators.
doc.carousel.intro: Carousels scroll a set of items with Material keyline sizes: large, medium, and small masks keep media at full width for a parallax effect. Prefer multi-browse for browsing, hero for a focal feature, uncontained for same-size free scroll, and full-screen for vertical paging. Optional controls, page indicators, and loop wrap complete the pattern — no autoplay.
doc.carousel.section.hero.blurb: One large item with small peeks — align start or center.
doc.carousel.section.uncontained.blurb: Same-size items cut off at the edge — free scroll, no snap.
doc.carousel.section.fullscreen.blurb: One edge-to-edge item at a time — vertical snap.
doc.carousel.demo.label: Landscapes
doc.countdown.title: Countdown
doc.countdown.blurb: Timer — duration or end date · segment cells · auto-start.
doc.countdown.intro: Countdown displays remaining time until zero, either from an initial duration or a fixed end timestamp. Format the output string or use segments for separate HH/mm/ss cells with optional unit labels. Control playback with start, pause, and reset methods.
doc.countdown.section.endDate.blurb: Pick a target — the countdown ticks to that moment.
doc.countdown.section.duration.blurb: Fixed ms via time — inline format or segment cells.
doc.marquee.title: Marquee
doc.marquee.blurb: Horizontal ticker — infinite loop or classic pass · speed · pause on hover.
doc.marquee.intro: Marquees scroll slotted content horizontally for tickers and credits. Choose infinite duplication or a classic one-pass animation, tune duration or speed, and pause on hover when users need to read the text.
doc.confetti.title: Confetti
doc.confetti.blurb: Canvas bursts — presets from the canvas-confetti gallery · vendored engine (no npm dep).
doc.confetti.intro: Confetti celebrates success states with particle bursts. The engine is a TypeScript port of Kiril Vatev’s canvas-confetti, shipped inside K3ui so you never add that package. Use fire(), named presets (basic, random, school pride, fireworks, snow…), or custom SVG path shapes. Reduced motion is honored by default.
doc.confetti.section.presets.blurb: Gallery demos inspired by kirilv.com/canvas-confetti — click to fire.
doc.sound-fx.title: Sound FX
doc.sound-fx.blurb: Interaction sounds — click · hover · enter · leave · mute SFX (not music).
doc.sound-fx.intro: Sound FX plays short UI cues from mp3/ogg (or wav) files when elements declare data-k3-sound-click, data-k3-sound-hover, data-k3-sound-enter, or data-k3-sound-leave. Mute is stored separately from the music player so users can silence clicks without stopping a playlist. Prefer reduced noise: mute control is keyboard-accessible and hover sounds wait for a first user gesture (autoplay policy).
doc.audio-player.title: Audio player
doc.audio-player.blurb: Playlist — card · compact · toolbar · sticky · phone · full · seek · shapes · hotkeys.
doc.audio-player.intro: Media player for mp3/ogg playlists. Six variants: card, compact, toolbar, sticky, phone, and full (queue + lyrics). Prefer the phone variant on smartphones. Wavy seek, Material shape morph, dynamic color from cover seed, expandable sheet, and Space/←→/N/P/M hotkeys when enabled.
doc.audio-player.section.card.blurb: Morph cover · wavy seek · like / expand. Hotkeys on the card demo only.
doc.audio-player.section.toolbar.blurb: Click cover / title to dock in the content area (never over the rail). Click again to return here (demo only). Shuffle · repeat · playlist (list expands upward).
doc.audio-player.section.phone.blurb: Vertical template · queue / lyrics in a bottom sheet. On smartphone, prefer this variant over card / toolbar / full.
doc.audio-player.section.full.blurb: Two columns — now playing + Up next / Lyrics. Opt-in skip ±15/30 · share · download · oscillation seek.
doc.qr-code.title: QR code
doc.qr-code.blurb: Styled QR — dots · corners · colors · logo · SVG via qr-code-styling.
doc.qr-code.intro: QR codes encode a URL or short payload as a scannable matrix. Style modules and finder patterns with qr-code-styling (rounded, dots, classy, …), tint with theme roles or custom colors, and optionally place a center logo. Prefer SVG for crisp scaling; download PNG when you need a raster asset.
doc.qr-code.section.playground.blurb: Edit the value — the code updates live.
doc.qr-code.section.generator.blurb: Live preview — shape · dots · eyes · logo PNG · colors.
doc.qr-code.section.colors.blurb: Theme roles or any CSS color via dots-color.
doc.qr-code.hint.circle: Body / eye / ball SVG patterns. shape="circle" = decorative silhouette (not Messenger / App Clip / Kik).
qrcode.label: QR code
doc.breadcrumb.title: Breadcrumb
doc.breadcrumb.blurb: Trail — plain · tonal · filled · chevron/slash/dot separators · collapse.
doc.breadcrumb.intro: Breadcrumbs show hierarchy and the current page within a trail. Supply items as JSON with optional icons and links, pick variant and separator style, and collapse long paths after N visible crumbs. Non-current items emit k3-select for SPA routing.
doc.pagination.title: Pagination
doc.pagination.blurb: Numeric pages — ellipsis · first/prev/next/last · sibling window.
doc.pagination.intro: Pagination navigates paged content with numbered buttons and optional first, previous, next, and last controls. Set total page count and current page; ellipsis compresses long ranges. Each change emits k3-change with the new 1-based page.
doc.pagination-alpha.title: Pagination Alpha
doc.pagination-alpha.blurb: A–Z index strip — counts · horizontal or vertical · disabled letters.
doc.pagination-alpha.intro: Alphabetical pagination jumps lists by first letter. Pass item labels to derive counts per letter, highlight the active letter, and hide or disable empty letters. Selection emits k3-select with the chosen letter.
doc.index-list.title: Index list
doc.index-list.blurb: Grouped directory — sticky headers · A–Z rail · scroll spy.
doc.index-list.intro: Index lists group long directories by letter with sticky section headers and an optional scrub rail. Provide items as JSON or slotted rows; scrollToKey jumps to a section and k3-section-change tracks the visible group.
doc.scroll-to-top.hint.shell: Live control is docked bottom-end (left of the GitHub FAB) — scroll this pane to reveal the circular progress ring.
doc.scroll-to-top.title: Scroll to top
doc.scroll-to-top.blurb: Floating control — threshold · progress ring · smooth scroll.
doc.scroll-to-top.intro: Scroll to top appears after the user scrolls past a threshold and returns the viewport to the top on click. Optional progress ring reflects scroll depth; tune size, offsets, and animation duration to match your FAB stack.
doc.app-bar.title: App bars
doc.app-bar.blurb: Small · medium flexible · large flexible — optional sticky.
doc.app-bar.intro: Top app bars frame a screen with navigation and actions. Small bars stay compact; medium and large flexible bars grow with title and subtitle. Optional sticky keeps the bar pinned while content scrolls. Place leading navigation, a concise headline, and trailing icon actions that stay within the touch target.
doc.footer-bar.title: Footer bar
doc.footer-bar.blurb: Bottom bar — optional sticky bottom + FAB slot.
doc.footer-bar.intro: Footer bars host persistent bottom actions and an optional FAB. Use them for primary next steps on long forms or media screens. Sticky footers stay pinned while the pane scrolls; keep actions few and clearly labeled.
doc.split-button.title: Buttons Split
doc.split-button.blurb: M3E — leading + trailing menu (≥2 items) · gap 2dp · five sizes (32–136) · filled|tonal|outlined|elevated.
doc.split-button.intro: Split buttons combine a primary action with a trailing menu of related alternatives. Put the most common action on the leading segment and at least two menu items on the trailing side. Five Expressive sizes and filled, tonal, outlined, or elevated variants keep the control aligned with nearby buttons.
doc.text-field.title: Text fields
doc.text-field.blurb: Outlined · filled · standard — floating or static label, clear, icons.
doc.text-field.intro: Text fields collect short user input. Outlined is the default for forms, filled suits denser surfaces, and standard (underline) stays the quietest. Pair labels, supporting text, and error text carefully; use leading or trailing icons for search, clear, or validation, and never rely on placeholder alone for the field’s name.
doc.textarea.title: Text area
doc.textarea.blurb: Multiline — outlined · filled · standard, same chrome as text fields.
doc.textarea.intro: Text areas capture multiline content with the same chrome as text fields. Choose outlined, filled, or standard to match neighboring inputs, set a sensible rows default, and expose max-length when the backend enforces one. Keep supporting text for guidance, not for repeating the label.
doc.field-group.title: Field group
doc.field-group.blurb: Fieldset + legend — wraps standard K3ui fields (floating labels).
doc.field-group.intro: Field groups wrap related inputs in a fieldset with a legend so assistive tech announces the shared context. Use them for address blocks, credentials, or any cluster that shares validation. Errors on the group should explain the whole set; field-level errors stay on the individual control.
doc.pin-field.title: PIN / OTP
doc.pin-field.blurb: Per-character cells — numeric · alpha · alphanumeric, mask, groups.
doc.pin-field.intro: PIN and OTP fields collect fixed-length codes one character at a time. Pick numeric, alpha, or alphanumeric charsets to match the source, enable masking for secrets, and group cells when codes are spoken in chunks. Autofocus the first empty cell and move focus forward as the user types.
doc.select.title: Select
doc.select.blurb: Exposed dropdown — k3-text-field trigger (outlined · filled · standard).
doc.select.intro: Select exposes a dropdown of predefined options behind a text-field-style trigger. Prefer it over free text when the value set is closed. Keep option labels scannable, support keyboard open/close, and match outlined, filled, or standard to the rest of the form.
doc.checkbox.title: Checkbox
doc.checkbox.intro: Checkboxes toggle independent options on or off, including an indeterminate state for partial selection in trees and bulk actions. Pair each box with a clear label, group related boxes, and avoid using a single checkbox as the only way to submit a form.
doc.radio.title: Radio
doc.radio.blurb: Single choice — scale from a perfectly centered inner dot.
doc.radio.intro: Radio buttons let people pick exactly one option from a short list. Keep the set small, share a name across the group, and place the selected indicator so it stays visually centered. Prefer a select when the list grows beyond a handful of choices.
doc.switch.title: Switch
doc.switch.intro: Switches turn a single setting on or off with immediate effect. Use them for preferences that apply instantly — not for actions that need confirmation. Label the setting, not the state words “on/off”, and keep switches out of dense form rows where a checkbox would read more clearly.
doc.chip.title: Chips
doc.chip.blurb: Assist · filter · input · suggestion — elevated, chip-set, avatar, status tones.
doc.chip.intro: Chips represent compact entities or filters: assist for actions, filter for refining results, input for removable entries, and suggestion for system prompts. Elevate when they need lift on busy surfaces, use chip-sets for multi or exclusive selection, and reserve status tones for semantic labels — not notification badges.
doc.chip.section.types.blurb: Assist · filter · input · suggestion — four contexts.
doc.chip.section.status.blurb: Colored label pills (table Available / Unavailable) — not notification badges.
doc.chip.section.elevated.blurb: Assist · filter · suggestion — elevation 1, no outline. Input stays flat.
doc.chip.section.set.blurb: Group with multi or exclusive selection · arrow keys.
doc.chip.section.sortable.blurb: Drag to reorder — shared attachSortable / K3UI.dnd.
doc.chip.section.input.blurb: Clearable — pad start 16 · end 8. With avatar 24 — pad start 4.
doc.chip.section.forced.blurb: Semantic status — success · error · info · note · warning.
doc.chip.section.filter.blurb: Container · label · leading icon · trailing icon.
doc.chip.legend.label: Label text
doc.slider.title: Slider
doc.slider.blurb: M3 Expressive · standard · centered · range · toolbar · XS–XL · stops · inset icon.
doc.slider.intro: Sliders select from a continuous or discrete range. Prefer standard for most cases; centered when values cross a midpoint; range for a min–max pair (horizontal only — avoid vertical range). Toolbar mirrors the audio-player volume pill (mute + slider). MD+ standard can host an inset icon that moves between active and inactive track. Keep a large enough handle for touch.
doc.slider.section.playground.blurb: Horizontal and vertical side by side · size · stops · inset icon · label · indicator · ± · toolbar.
doc.slider.control.label: Label
doc.rating.title: Rating
doc.rating.blurb: Stars · half steps · sizes · theme or custom colors · readonly.
doc.rating.intro: Ratings collect a score on a discrete scale (usually 1–5 stars). Use half steps when finer grain helps. Prefer theme color roles for brand consistency, or set active-color / inactive-color (and CSS vars) when the product needs a fixed accent. Mark reviews as readonly when the value is display-only.
doc.rating.section.sizes.blurb: XS · SM · MD · LG · XL — icon optical size.
doc.rating.section.colors.blurb: Theme roles or any CSS color via active-color / inactive-color.
doc.rating.section.icons.blurb: icon / icon-active ligatures, or unchecked / checked slots.
doc.date-picker.title: Date picker
doc.date-picker.blurb: Calendar · docked or modal · single or range · min/max.
doc.date-picker.intro: Date pickers present a temporary surface for choosing a date or range with month, year, and multi-year views. Docked anchors to a field; modal shows a headline. Pair a text field with k3-date-picker-toggle, then confirm with OK.
doc.date-picker.hint: Short range: 2 months + one wide field. Long range: 1 month + Start/End fields, each with its own calendar icon.
doc.mood-calendar.title: Mood Calendar
doc.mood-calendar.blurb: Year grid · legend · journal (dialog) · stats — current year + n−1.
doc.mood-calendar.intro: Mood Calendar visualizes a year of journal days as a color grid. Tap a day to open the journal in a modal dialog, filter via the legend, and read yearly stats. Demo tabs cover the current year and the previous year; pass your own entries from the app.
doc.time-picker.title: Time picker
doc.time-picker.blurb: Dial · keyboard — 12/24h · docked or modal · min/max.
doc.time-picker.intro: Time pickers present a temporary surface for choosing a time with a clock dial or keyboard fields. Support 12-hour and 24-hour formats and min/max bounds. Docked mode anchors to the field like a menu and repositions when space is tight. Pair a text field with k3-time-picker-toggle to open the picker, then confirm with OK.
doc.time-picker.hint.orient: Docked anchors to the field · modal centers with scrim. Dial or keyboard input — toggle via the icon. Input auto-advances hour → minute.
doc.progress.title: Progress
doc.progress.intro: Progress indicators communicate ongoing work. Prefer determinate bars when you know completion percentage; use indeterminate or wavy expressive motion when duration is unknown. Oscillation (linear) decodes real PCM from src — same peaks cache as the audio seek. Keep them near the content they describe and announce status changes to assistive tech.
doc.loading.title: Loading indicator
doc.loading.intro: Loading indicators show that the UI is busy without implying a known percentage. Use the morphing shape for brand moments and the contained variant inside buttons or tight slots. Prefer skeleton screens for longer waits where layout can be previewed.
doc.skeleton.title: Skeleton
doc.skeleton.blurb: Loading placeholder — wave shimmer (default) · soft pulse · shapes.
doc.skeleton.intro: Skeletons placeholder content while data loads. Wave shimmer is the default; pulse is quieter. Match bone shapes to the real UI, wrap live content so loaded can reveal it in place, and avoid skeletons that last longer than a short network wait.
doc.skeleton.section.reveal.blurb: Wrap the real UI — bone covers it while loading, then loaded reveals it.
doc.skeleton.section.bones.blurb: Empty bones (no slot) — sizing only; they stay as placeholders (not toggled).
doc.skeleton.demo.name: Jane Doe
doc.skeleton.demo.card.title: Profile card
doc.skeleton.demo.card.body: Content appears when the skeleton is marked loaded.
doc.snackbar.title: Snackbar
doc.snackbar.blurb: 1–2 lines · action · dismiss · queue · short/long/indefinite — inverse surface (M3 / Android).
doc.snackbar.intro: Snackbars confirm brief outcomes at the bottom of the screen. Keep copy to one or two lines, offer at most one action, and choose short, long, or indefinite duration with care. Use the inverse surface so the message stays readable over any page chrome.
doc.snackbar.demo.twoline: The item already has the label “travel.” Add a new label.
doc.alert.title: Alert
doc.alert.blurb: Callout-style · accent bar · variants · shapes · dismissible.
doc.alert.intro: Alerts are supporting containers for contextual or supplemental information — icon, label, and body with a leading accent bar (M3E Callout model). Use theme variants for brand emphasis and semantic tones (success · warning · info · error · note) for status. Prefer rounded shapes; square when the layout needs flush edges. Add dismissible when the message can be cleared.
doc.alert.section.variants.blurb: Theme roles and semantic tones — container + accent bar.
doc.alert.section.actions.blurb: Trailing action slot next to the body.
doc.alert.demo.body: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Supplemental details stay in the body.
doc.dialog.title: Dialog
doc.dialog.blurb: Basic (centered) · fullscreen on compact only (<600) — adapts to basic ≥600 (M3). Elevates above the nav rail.
doc.dialog.intro: Dialogs focus attention on a decision or short task. Use basic centered dialogs for confirms; fullscreen only on compact widths under 600 dp, adapting back to basic on larger breakpoints. Keep titles short, actions clear, and elevate above navigation so the rail never covers the sheet.
doc.dialog.demo.basic.title: Discard draft?
doc.dialog.demo.fs.title: New event
doc.dialog.demo.fs.hint: Full-screen on compact (<600). On larger widths this swaps to a basic dialog — Save moves to the footer (M3 Adaptive). Do not offset under the nav rail.
doc.tooltip.title: Tooltip
doc.tooltip.blurb: Plain or rich (header + actions) — top · bottom · left · right · start · end + corners.
doc.tooltip.intro: Tooltips explain a control on hover or focus. Plain tips carry a short phrase; rich tips add a headline and optional actions for denser help. Anchor to eight sides plus logical start/end so RTL mirrors correctly, and never put essential information only in a tooltip.
doc.badge.title: Badge
doc.badge.blurb: Dot · count · 999+ — four corners (logical or physical).
doc.badge.intro: Badges draw attention to status on an icon or avatar — a dot for presence, a count for quantity, and 999+ when the number overflows. Position with logical corners so RTL mirrors, or physical left/right when the layout must stay fixed. Do not use badges as colored status pills; those belong to chips.
doc.badge.section.sizes.blurb: Small dot, large digit, and max characters (999+).
doc.badge.section.corners.blurb: Logical top/bottom × start/end (RTL mirrors). Physical left/right stay fixed.
doc.badge.legend.dot: Small badge on a navigation item
doc.badge.legend.large: Large badge on a navigation item
doc.badge.legend.max: Large badge with max characters on a navigation item
doc.badge.section.note.blurb: Colored Available / Unavailable labels are chips — see Chips → Status.
doc.avatar.title: Avatars
doc.avatar.blurb: Image · initials · status badge · stacked / grid groups — sm · md · lg. LTR/RTL aware.
doc.avatar.intro: Avatars identify people or entities with an image, initials, or both. Add presence status when online state matters, stack or grid groups for teams, and keep sizes sm · md · lg consistent in a view. Interactive avatars can open menus; respect LTR/RTL for badge and stack direction.
doc.card.title: Cards
doc.card.blurb: Filled · outlined · elevated — media, avatar, pricing, horizontal, collection DnD.
doc.card.intro: Cards group related content and actions. Filled suits quiet containers, outlined adds a border for separation, and elevated lifts primary content. Interactive cards can morph the border on hover; media slots work best with cover-fit imagery and a clear headline.
doc.menu.title: Menus
doc.menu.blurb: Vertical Expressive · baseline · standard / vibrant · gaps · density 0…−3. Enter/exit: opacity (spatial-fast) from the trigger; submenus match after placement.
doc.menu.intro: Menus list actions or options from a trigger. Prefer vertical Expressive for new UI, with standard or vibrant color, density steps, and optional supporting text — not nested controls. Animate enter/exit with opacity and scale from the trigger; submenus follow the same motion after placement.
doc.menu.section.density.blurb: On web, density levels control spacing between elements. Increasing density decreases top and bottom padding (0 = default, −3 = densest).
doc.menu.section.supporting.blurb: M3’s caution is about nested actions (buttons, switches), not a second text line. Use the supporting-text slot — one action per item.
doc.list.title: Lists
doc.list.blurb: M3 Expressive — standard · segmented · selection · expand · DnD.
doc.list.intro: Lists are continuous vertical indexes of text and images. Prefer segmented Expressive (2 dp gaps, outer 24 / inner 4 radii, shape morph on hover and select). Use leading slots for icon, avatar, image, or video; trailing for chevron, checkbox, radio, or meta. Selection modes: single (radio), multiple (checkbox), or hide the indicator. Row expand (details or nested list) stays on List — Accordion belongs to Expansion panel.
doc.tabs.title: Tabs
doc.tabs.intro: Tabs organize peer views at the same hierarchy. Primary tabs pair icons with a short indicator; secondary tabs underline the full cell for text-only sets. Keep tab counts manageable, preserve selection when content swaps, and avoid nesting tabs inside tabs.
doc.nav-rail.title: Navigation Rail
doc.nav-rail.blurb: Mid / expanded (≥600dp). Collapsed/Expanded · header FAB · menu / menu_open · FILL.
doc.nav-rail.intro: Navigation rails suit mid-width and expanded layouts (≥600 dp). Collapse or expand destinations, optionally lead with a FAB, and use menu / menu_open affordances when the rail can hide. Keep destination labels short and the active item obvious with FILL icons when selected.
doc.table.title: Tables
doc.table.blurb: material.io style — header tint, status chips, resource links.
doc.table.intro: Tables present structured data with clear headers, alignment, and optional status chips. Use outlined or filled surfaces, keep numeric columns end-aligned, and prefer resource links for external references. Generated rows work well for token dumps; handcrafted markup suits rowspan and rich cells.
doc.sheet.title: Sheets
doc.sheet.blurb: Bottom (640 dp or full) · side — modal, 48 dp handle, M3 drag dismiss (56 dp / 125 dp/s), open/close lifecycle.
doc.sheet.intro: Sheets present supplementary surfaces — bottom sheets at 640 dp or full height, and side sheets for wider layouts. Use a 48 dp drag handle, modal scrim when focus must stay in the sheet, and clear open/close lifecycle hooks so the host page restores scroll and focus.
doc.colors.title: Color
doc.colors.blurb: Dynamic color — SchemeExpressive (M3E 2025/26) system roles, tonal palettes.
doc.color-roles.title: Roles
doc.color-roles.blurb: MaterialDynamicColors system roles — live CSS vars after theme.apply.
doc.color-roles.intro: System color roles are the Material Dynamic Color contracts your components consume — primary, surface, on-surface, and friends. After theme.apply they map to live CSS variables. Prefer roles over raw hex so light/dark and seed changes stay coherent.
doc.color-palettes.title: Palettes
doc.color-palettes.blurb: Core tonal ladders (0–100) for the current seed and scheme variant.
doc.color-palettes.intro: Tonal palettes expose the 0–100 ladders behind the current seed and scheme variant. Use them to understand contrast steps and to pick custom accents that still sit on the dynamic scale. Changing the seed regenerates every tone live in the playground.
doc.color-extras.title: Additional colors
doc.color-extras.blurb: Static reference ladders (--k3-ref-palette-*) — local accents without replacing the dynamic theme.
doc.color-extras.intro: Static reference palettes (--k3-ref-palette-*) give local accents without replacing the dynamic theme. Reach for them when a chart series or brand chip must stay fixed while the rest of the UI follows the seed.
doc.color-lab.copy-hint: Click a swatch to copy HEX · Alt+click to copy the CSS variable.
doc.elevation.title: Elevation
doc.elevation.blurb: Levels 0–5 — shadow stacks + surface tint for tonal lift.
doc.elevation.intro: Elevation levels 0–5 combine shadow stacks with surface tint for tonal lift. Use lower levels for resting surfaces and higher ones for temporary overlays. Prefer tokens and .k3-elevation-* utilities over hand-authored box-shadows so dark mode stays correct.
doc.icons.title: Icons
doc.icons.blurb: Material Symbols — sizes 20·24·40·48, FILL / wght / GRAD / opsz axes.
doc.icons.intro: Material Symbols power every ligature icon in K3ui. Prefer data-k3-icon with notranslate markup, keep names in the playground font subset, and tune FILL / wght / GRAD / opsz axes via tokens. Never put spaces inside a ligature name or Chrome Translate will break the glyph.
doc.motion.title: Motion
doc.motion.blurb: Expressive spatial & effects — durations, easings, reduced-motion.
doc.motion.intro: Motion tokens cover Expressive spatial and effects durations, easings, and springs. Honor prefers-reduced-motion and data-k3-reduce-motion so animations ease or disable. Use motion to clarify hierarchy — not to decorate every state change.
doc.nav-bar.title: Navigation Bar
doc.nav-bar.blurb: Compact (<600dp). Icon pill expands center→sides · vertical|horizontal.
doc.nav-bar.intro: Navigation bars serve compact layouts under 600 dp. Destinations use an expanding icon pill — vertical or horizontal — so the active item stays readable. Limit to a handful of top-level destinations and keep labels visible whenever space allows.
doc.toolbar.title: Toolbar
doc.toolbar.blurb: M3E — docked or floating · standard / vibrant · pair with FAB.
doc.toolbar.intro: Material 3 Expressive toolbars replace the bottom app bar with two variants: docked (full-width strip) and floating (elevated pill, horizontal or vertical). Use vibrant color for emphasis. Slots hold icon buttons, buttons, or text fields; pair a FAB with an 8 dp gap. Do not show a toolbar at the same time as a navigation bar.

doc.doc-nav.title: Prev Next
doc.doc-nav.blurb: Previous / Up next cards — M3 documentation pager on the layout grid.
doc.doc-nav.intro: Prev / next cards page documentation along the layout grid. Use clear titles for the adjacent topics so readers can jump without returning to the nav rail. Keep the control full-width in the doc container and consistent across component pages.
doc.shapes.title: Shape
doc.shapes.blurb: Corner scale (none→full) + 35 expressive unit SVG shapes.
doc.shapes.intro: Shape tokens scale corners from none to full and ship 35 expressive unit SVGs. Apply corner roles to surfaces and controls so morphing press states stay on-brand. Prefer tokens over one-off border-radius values.
doc.spacing.title: Spacing
doc.spacing.blurb: space100 = 8dp baseline — full scale + layout gutter / margins.
doc.spacing.intro: Spacing follows an 8 dp baseline (space100) through space0…900, plus layout gutter and margins. Use these tokens for padding and gaps instead of hard-coded rem values so density and breakpoints stay aligned with Material 3.
doc.typography.title: Typography
doc.typography.blurb: Type scale display→label — size, line-height, weight, tracking, emphasized.
doc.typography.intro: The type scale runs from display to label with size, line-height, weight, tracking, and emphasized styles. Apply .k3-* type classes or tokens so headings and body copy stay consistent across locales and density modes.
